parts.title: Grandfather's chess set
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
Every Saturday afternoon, my grandfather and I sit at the kitchen table and play chess. It is our special time. The chess set is very old, with wooden pieces that he made himself when he was a young man. One of the knights has a small crack in its head because I dropped it when I was five.

Grandfather learned the game from his own father in a small village in Poland. He says that chess is like life: you cannot move backwards, and every choice has a result. When I was little, I did not understand this, but now I think that I do.

At first, he won every game. I got angry and sometimes I threw a piece across the table. He never laughed at me. Instead, he showed me how to look at the board in a different way, thinking about what my opponent might do next.

Last month, I won a game for the very first time. Grandfather clapped his hands and said, "Now you are not just my grandson, you are my equal." I have never felt so proud. We are going to play again this Saturday, and I hope to win once more.

parts.title: The story of chess
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
Chess is one of the oldest games in the world. [1] People first played it in India about fifteen hundred years ago, and the game then travelled along trade routes to Persia and Europe.

In the beginning, the pieces looked very different from the ones that we know today. [2] They were made to look like soldiers, elephants and horses, because the game was a small battle.

Over the centuries, the rules changed several times. [3] In the fifteenth century, the queen became the most powerful piece on the board, and the game became much faster.

Today, millions of people play chess, from children at school to famous champions. [4] Many of them play online against people from other countries.

Chess is also good for the brain. [5] Teachers say that pupils who play chess often get better marks in maths.
sentences: Experts say that it makes players think carefully and plan.
Nobody was allowed to play it without the king's permission.
Those early rules were written down by monks.
In fact, the internet has made the game more popular than ever.
Even now, the king is the weakest piece in the game.
Its history is much longer than that of most sports.
One of these changes is still the biggest in the history of the game.
Some of the early pieces were also made of ivory.

gaps.explanation: Its long history leads to the sentence about the first players in India.
Some early pieces were made of ivory, and the next sentence says they looked like soldiers and animals.
"These changes" are the rule changes in the sentence before; the next sentence gives the biggest one, the new queen.
The internet made the game more popular, and many people play online.
Experts say that chess makes players think and plan, and teachers say it helps maths marks.

parts.title: A talk about chess
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: roxana
turns.text: Good evening, everyone. Tonight I would like to tell you a little about chess, a game that is more than fifteen hundred years old. Many people think it is only for clever people, but anyone can learn it. Let’s start with the board. It has eight rows and eight columns, and some beginners think that makes sixty squares, but in fact it is sixty-four, half of them black and half white. At the beginning of a game, each player has sixteen pieces, so there are thirty-two on the board together. There are six different kinds. Now, which piece matters most? Many newcomers guess it is the queen, because she moves so far, but they are wrong. You can lose your queen and still win. If you lose your king, the game is over, so he is the piece that you protect above all. The most powerful piece, though, really is the queen. The rook and the bishop can travel far in a straight line too, but only the queen can go in any direction for as many squares as she likes. The knight is my favourite, because it jumps over other pieces and always surprises beginners. Next, time. At home, you can think for as long as you like, even an hour for one move! But in serious tournaments each player has a limited time, and it is controlled with clocks. You press a button after each move and the other side’s time starts to run. Some people use their phone as a timer, but at official events you are not allowed to. Finally, how do you improve? Reading books helps, and a computer program can teach you a lot, but it will beat you every time, which is not much fun. For me the best way is to play against friends, especially friends who are better than you. You will lose often at first, but you learn something from every game. Thank you for listening, and now, who would like to try a game?

gaps.explanation: Beginners think there are sixty squares, but she says it is sixty-four.

gaps.prompt: The number of pieces on the board when a game begins
gaps.explanation: Each player has sixteen pieces, so there are thirty-two together.

gaps.prompt: The piece that a player must protect above all
gaps.explanation: You can lose the queen and still win, but if you lose the king the game is over.

gaps.prompt: The strongest piece on the board
gaps.explanation: The rook and the bishop travel far, but only the queen can go in any direction as far as she likes.

gaps.prompt: In serious tournaments, thinking time is controlled with
gaps.explanation: At official events they use clocks, not a phone timer.

gaps.explanation: Books and computer programs help, but the best way is to play against friends.

parts.title: An interview with a puzzle maker
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Delroy, you make crosswords for a national newspaper. How did your first one get printed?

turns.speaker: p
turns.text: Ha, that’s a funny story. I was fourteen and made a crossword for fun. My mother wanted to post it to the paper, but I said no, I was too shy. In the end my English teacher found it in my bag. She liked it, wrote a letter and sent it in herself. I didn’t know until I saw it in print.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: What is the hardest part of making a crossword?

turns.speaker: p
turns.text: People think it’s drawing the grid, and yes, that takes time, I use a ruler and a pencil. Writing the solution at the end is boring, but it’s just copying. The real challenge is the clues. A good clue must be clever but fair, and I can spend a whole evening on just one.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: And where do you write down your ideas?

turns.speaker: p
turns.text: They come everywhere: on the bus, in a cafe. For years I used my phone, but I lost it twice, and the notes with it. I also bought a large board for my wall once, but it was too big for my flat, so my brother has it now. These days I carry a small notebook in my pocket.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: You once made a mistake in a puzzle. Why do you check everything twice now?

turns.speaker: p
turns.text: Oh, that was a terrible week. One clue had two possible answers. Many readers wrote to the newspaper, some of them quite angry. The editor was very kind and didn’t stop my column, he just laughed. And my mother said nothing, she doesn’t do crosswords. But I felt so embarrassed that I now check every answer twice.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: You walk your dog every evening. Is that for the dog?

turns.speaker: p
turns.text: Not really. He’s only three and he runs in the garden all day. And no, the doctor hasn’t ordered me to walk, though he’d approve. The truth is that after hours with words, my head is full. Walking is the only time it goes quiet, and often a new idea comes.

turns.speaker: i
turns.text: Finally, what would you say to someone who wants to start?

turns.speaker: p
turns.text: Don’t worry about studying maths, I didn’t, and you don’t need a degree. Some people say you must work in the morning, but I write at night and I’m fine. My advice is to make little puzzles and show them to your friends first. They will tell you honestly if a clue is boring or impossible.

questions.prompt: Where does Delroy keep his ideas now?
questions.explanation: He lost his phone twice and the board was too big, so he carries a notebook in his pocket.

questions.prompt: Why does Delroy check every answer twice now?
options: The editor stopped his column once
His mother found an error in print
Many readers wrote about one clue
questions.explanation: The editor did not stop his column and his mother said nothing; many readers wrote about a clue with two answers, so he felt embarrassed.

questions.prompt: Why does Delroy walk his dog every evening?
options: It clears his head after a day of words
The dog needs a lot of exercise
questions.explanation: The dog runs in the garden and the doctor has not ordered it; walking makes his head quiet after hours with words.

questions.prompt: What advice does Delroy give to beginners?
options: Show little puzzles to friends first
questions.explanation: He says maths and a degree are not needed and he writes at night; he advises showing little puzzles to friends first.

parts.title: Getting to know you
parts.instructions: Answer each question in your own words. Aim to speak for 20-30 seconds.

questions.prompt: Do you like playing games with your family? Which ones?
What do you usually do on a rainy day?
Are you good at solving problems? Why or why not?
Do you prefer working alone or in a team?
